sources.title: Anil Kerai, hermes-squad, docs/02-context-engineering.md, commit of 12 November 2026 (GitHub)

quotes.text: Every Kanban worker is a new process with an empty window.
The card body is the prompt.
Ambiguity left in a card gets resolved by a guess, which copies into every child, or by a block.
The reviewer re-runs the Verify commands; the engineer never marks its own homework.
Prefer a mechanism to a sentence.
Context size costs more than model tier.
A handoff summary is a compression boundary.
three roles started with a stale copy of the default's memory
Set each per role and clear inherited memory.
Create a new profile when a role needs different tools, credentials, model or risk rules. Use a skill when only the knowledge differs
AGENTS.md is a pointer, so workers get "read CLAUDE.md", not the rules
Agents propose, humans promote.

quotes.text: In our comparisons across several enterprise deployments, a single agent with skills frequently outperformed both the one-prompt-for-everything design and the subagent design on quality
